This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court passed the following:
 ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 21.01.2016 passed by III Additional Member, MACT, Sehore, District Sehore in MCC No. 33/2015 by which the claim filed by the deceased Nannulal has been dismissed on the ground that the claimants have failed to prove that the injured/deceased Nannulal had suffered an injury in the road accident in question.

2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in short, are that the injured Nannulal filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act on the ground that he was traveling in the offending bus.
Because of rash and negligent driving of the driver, the bus turned up side down on 22.05.2012, as a result, he sustained grievous injuries.
3. During the pendency of the claim petition, the claimant Nannulal expired and accordingly, the present appellants were impleaded as his legal representatives.

The Claims Tribunal after appreciating the evidence has come to a conclusion that the appellants have failed to prove that the claimant/deceased Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question.

4. Challenging the award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellants that it is clear from the medical documents that the injured Nannulal has suffered injuries on 22.05.2012 in a road accident, therefore, the Claims Tribunal has committed a material illegality by holding that the appellants have failed to prove that the injured Nannulal has suffered the injuries in the accident in question.

5. Per contra, it is submitted by the counsel for the respondents that since the injured has expired during the pendency of the claim petition, therefore, the claim petition so far as it relates to the recovery of compensation for the injures sustained by Nannulal would stand abated.

To buttress his contentions, the counsel for the respondents has relied upon the judgement passed by the a Full Nannulal (Dead) Through Lrs. Smt. ... vs Kashiram Maithil on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92967299/

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties.

7. The first question for consideration is as to whether the appellants had successfully proved that Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question or not?
8.

The appellants have filed a copy of the charge-sheet (Ex.-P/1), list of witnesses cited by the police in the charge-sheet (Ex.-P/2), copy of Dehatinalishi (Ex.-P/3), copy of FIR (Ex.-P/4), crime details from (Ex.-P/5), seizure of bus and other documents (Ex.-P/6) and the arrest memo of the driver (Ex.-P/7) and in none of the documents the name of Nannulal is mentioned.
Even the MLC of Nannulal has not been placed on record.
9. It is submitted by the counsel for the appellants that Nannulal had expired on 18.06.2013.
The claim petition was filed on 29.01.2013 whereas he expired on 18.06.2013.
From the final report Ex.-P/1, it is clear that it was filed on 05.07.2012 i.e. during the lifetime of Nannulal.
Therefore, if Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question, then his MLC as well as his name as a witness should have been there in the charge-sheet itself.
Even the statement of Nannulal recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. has not been filed.
Except the medical documents there is nothing to indicate that Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question.

10. Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the appellants have failed to prove that Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question.

11. So far as the abatement of the claim petition is concerned, it is true that Nannulal had expired during the pendency of the Claim Petition, but the claim for personal injury suffered by Nannulal would abate and the appellants can always prosecute the Claim Petition for pecuniary loss to the estate of the claimant.
Therefore, the entire claim petition had not abated on the death of Nannulal.
12. Since, the appellants have failed to prove that Nannulal had suffered injuries in the accident in question, therefore, no interference is required in the present appeal.

13. As a consequence thereof, the award dated 21.01.2016 passed by III Additional Member, MACT,
Sehore, District Sehore in MCC No. 33/2015 is hereby affirmed.
14. The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE ashish ASHISH KUMAR LILHARE 2023.02.23 14:41:45 +05'30'
